items.title: Reorganizing Six Into Three: Integrity, Essence, and Two Directions of Benefit

items.zh: 謂於是中，世尊顯示戒蘊略義，有三種相。一者、無失壞相，二者、自性相，三者、自性功德相。此復云何？謂若說言：安住具戒。由此顯示尸羅律儀無失壞相。若復說言：能善守護別解律儀。由此顯示尸羅律儀自性相。若復說言：軌則、所行皆悉圓滿。由此顯示別解律儀，如其所受，觀他增上自性功德相。所以者何？由他觀見如是軌則、所行圓滿，未信者信，信者增長。由是發生清淨信處，心無厭惡，言不譏毀。若異於此具足尸羅軌則、所行皆圓滿者，觀他增上所有功德勝利，應無。與此相違過失，應有。若復說言：於微小罪見大怖畏、受學學處。由此顯示別解律儀，如其所受，觀自增上自性功德相。
items.en: Among these, the Bhagavat reveals the essential meaning of the aggregate of discipline through three marks: the mark of being free of loss or impairment; the mark of intrinsic nature; and the mark of intrinsic virtue. …When it is said "abiding in complete discipline," this reveals the mark of moral restraint being free of loss or impairment. When it is said "skilfully guarding the prātimokṣa restraint," this reveals the mark of moral restraint's intrinsic nature. When it is said "protocol and conduct are both entirely perfected," this reveals the mark of intrinsic virtue directed towards benefiting others, belonging to the prātimokṣa restraint as received. …When it is said "seeing great danger in even the slightest fault, and training in every point of training," this reveals the mark of intrinsic virtue directed towards benefiting oneself, belonging to the prātimokṣa restraint as received.

items.zh: 所以者何？雖由如是軌則、所行皆悉圓滿，獲得如前觀他增上功德勝利。然由毀犯淨戒因緣，當生惡趣；或無堪能得所未得，如前廣說。若能於彼微小罪中見大怖畏，於先所受上品學處能正修學。由是因緣，身壞已後當生善趣；亦有堪能得所未得，如前廣說。由是因緣，說此名為別解律儀，如其所受，觀自增上功德勝利。

items.title: A Second Threefold Lens: Receiving, Liberating, and Cultivating Discipline — and Ten Ways It Can Falter

items.zh: 復有異門。謂佛世尊此中略顯三種戒性。一、受持戒性，二、出離戒性，三、修習戒性。謂若說言：安住具戒。由此顯示受持戒性。若復說言：能善守護別解律儀。由此顯示出離戒性。所以者何？別解律儀所攝淨戒，當知說名增上戒學。即依如是增上戒學，修增上心、增上慧學；由此能得一切苦盡，究竟出離。如是出離，用增上戒以為前行所依止處，是故說此別解律儀名出離戒性。若復說言：軌則、所行皆悉圓滿，於微小罪見大怖畏，受學學處。由此顯示修習戒性。所以者何？若由如是所說諸相別解律儀，修習淨戒，名善修習、極善修習。如是一種尸羅律儀現前宣說，當知六種。又即如是尸羅律儀，由十因緣，當知虧損；即此相違十因緣故，當知圓滿。云何十種虧損因緣？一者、最初惡受尸羅律儀，二者、太極沈下，三者、大極浮散，四者、放逸懈怠所攝，五者、發起邪願，六者、軌則虧損所攝，七者、淨命虧損所攝，八者、墮在二邊，九者、不能出離，十者、所受失壞。
items.en: There is, further, another approach. The Bhagavat, in brief, reveals three natures of discipline here: the nature of receiving and upholding; the nature of leading to liberation; and the nature of ongoing cultivation. …The pure discipline comprised within the prātimokṣa restraint should be known as the higher training in discipline. Resting on this higher training in discipline, one cultivates the higher training in concentration and the higher training in wisdom; by this, one is able to exhaust all suffering and attain final liberation. Such liberation takes the higher training in discipline as its preliminary foundation — this is why the prātimokṣa restraint is called "the nature of leading to liberation." …Thus this single moral restraint, when set forth directly, should be understood as sixfold. Again, this same moral restraint, through ten causes and conditions, should be known to become impaired; and through the reverse of these same ten, should be known to become fulfilled. What are the ten causes of impairment? Wrongly receiving the moral restraint from the very start; being excessively lax; being excessively agitated; falling under heedlessness and laziness; giving rise to a misguided aspiration; impairment in protocol; impairment in one's pure livelihood; falling into one of two extremes; being unable to attain liberation; and letting what was received degrade entirely.

items.zh: 云何名為最初惡受尸羅律儀？

items.title: The First Four Ways Discipline Falters: Wrong Motive, Laxity, Agitation, and Unrepented Lapses

items.zh: 謂如有一，王所逼迫而求出家，或為狂賊之所逼迫、或為債主之所逼迫、或為怖畏之所逼迫、或不活畏之所逼迫而求出家。不為沙門性、不為婆羅門性、不為自調伏、不為自寂靜、不為自涅槃而求出家。如是名為最初惡受尸羅律儀。云何名為太極沈下？謂如有一，性無羞恥，惡作羸劣，為性慢緩，於諸學處所作慢緩。如是名為太極沈下。云何名為太極浮散？謂如有一，堅執惡取，非處惡作，於不應作諸惡作中浪作惡作；非處於他起輕蔑心、或惱害心，於其非處強生曉悟。如是名為太極浮散。云何放逸懈怠所攝？謂如有一，由過去世毀犯所犯；於此毀犯，由失念故，一類不能如法還淨。如由過去，由未來世、由現在世當知亦爾。
items.en: It is like one who seeks ordination coerced by a king, or by fierce bandits, or by a creditor, or by fear, or by fear of destitution — seeking ordination not for the sake of the recluse's nature, not for the sake of the brahmin's nature, not to subdue oneself, not to quiet oneself, not to attain nirvāṇa. This is called wrongly receiving the moral restraint from the very start. …It is like one who is, by nature, without shame, whose remorse is feeble and weak, who is by nature sluggish, sluggish in every point of training. This is called being excessively lax. …It is like one who firmly clings to wrong views, feels regret where none is warranted, needlessly regrets what should not be regretted, and, out of place, feels contempt or ill will towards others, forcibly insisting one understands where one does not — judging others to have transgressed where they have not. This is called being excessively agitated. …It is like one who, having transgressed in some past time, fails entirely, through loss of mindfulness, to restore purity in accordance with the Dharma regarding that transgression. As with the past, so too should it be understood regarding the future and the present.

items.zh: 謂毀犯所犯；於此毀犯，由失念故，一類不能如法還淨。又非先時，於所毀犯發起猛利無犯樂欲。謂我定當如如所行、如如所住，如是如是行於所行、如是如是住於所住，於所毀犯終不毀犯。由是因緣，隨所行住，如是如是毀犯所犯。由此成就前際俱行、後際俱行、中際俱行、先時所作及俱隨行所有放逸。

blocks.text: The treatise reorganises the six aspects into three marks, then three natures, then lists ten ways discipline can be impaired.

The six aspects combine into three marks: **freedom from impairment** (abiding in discipline), **intrinsic nature** (the prātimokṣa, each precept's own features), and **intrinsic virtue** (protocol, conduct, fear of faults, training). Venerable Miào Jìng: pure discipline is "a place where others' pure faith arises". Master Cháng Bǎi: protocol is the surface; one must also guard oneself so that the precepts lead to concentration.

Discipline is received and upheld; it leads to liberation; it is cultivated continually. Master Cháng Bǎi: the precepts are the foundation of the building; "higher" (增上) means both leading on to concentration and supreme.

Ten ways discipline falters: wrongly receiving it; excessive laxity; excessive agitation; heedlessness and laziness; misguided aspiration; impaired protocol; impaired livelihood; falling into the two extremes; inability to reach liberation; and letting what was received degrade.

items: **Wrong reception:** going forth "coerced by a king, bandits, a creditor, fear, or fear of destitution", not for the recluse's nature. Venerable Miào Jìng: not to seek the noble path.
**Excessive laxity:** too passive about the precepts, careless of lapses.
**Excessive agitation:** anxious scrupulosity without right understanding. Master Cháng Bǎi: imagining offences where there are none.
**Heedlessness:** regretting a past lapse without amending, or committing faults again. Master Cháng Bǎi: "past" here means past time, not a past life.

quiz.q: What three marks does the treatise say reveal the aggregate of discipline?
options: free of impairment, intrinsic nature, intrinsic virtue
quiz.why: "First, the mark of being free of loss or impairment; second, the mark of intrinsic nature; third, the mark of intrinsic virtue." Venerable Miào Jìng: the six items are combined into three marks — the essentials of the six.

quiz.q: Perfected protocol and conduct show the virtue "directed towards benefiting others." What does this mean, and what must be avoided, per the masters?
options: Miào Jìng: one's pure conduct becomes a place where others' faith arises; Cháng Bǎi: clinging too much to precepts leads to judging others like a lawyer
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "a place where pure faith arises" — your purity, your pure precepts and perfected protocol, are where others' pure faith arises. Master Cháng Bǎi: if one clings too much to precepts, one easily sees others' faults, acting like a lawyer who likes to judge others' precepts, and everyone avoids one.

quiz.q: Is achieving only the "for others" side enough, per Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: no — perfected protocol is surface; one must also benefit oneself, guarding oneself to improve life after life
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: one cannot stop at perfected protocol and conduct — that is the surface; one must also benefit oneself, guarding oneself so that through the precepts each life is better than the last.

quiz.q: What three natures of discipline does the treatise say the Buddha reveals?
options: receiving, leading to liberation, ongoing cultivation
quiz.why: "The Bhagavat, in brief, reveals three natures of discipline here: receiving and upholding; leading to liberation; and ongoing cultivation." Master Cháng Bǎi: the receiving nature means taking the precepts into one's heart and holding them.

quiz.q: Why is the prātimokṣa called "the nature of leading to liberation," and with what image, per Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: precepts are the foundation for escaping the three realms — like laying a building's foundation
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: in practice to escape the three realms, the precepts are the foundation — like laying a building's foundation; hence the prātimokṣa is called the nature of leading to liberation. The treatise: resting on higher discipline one cultivates higher mind and wisdom and ends all suffering.

quiz.q: By which ten causes does the treatise say moral restraint is impaired?
options: wrong reception, excessive laxity, excessive agitation, heedlessness and laziness, misguided aspiration, impaired protocol, impaired livelihood, two extremes, inability to liberate, degradation
quiz.why: "First, wrongly receiving the moral restraint; second, excessive laxity; third, excessive agitation; fourth, heedlessness and laziness; fifth, misguided aspiration; sixth, impaired protocol; seventh, impaired livelihood; eighth, falling into two extremes; ninth, inability to attain liberation; tenth, letting what was received degrade."

quiz.q: How do "excessive laxity" and "excessive agitation" differ, per the masters?
options: Cháng Bǎi: laxity is too passive an attitude, agitation is wrong thinking without right view; Miào Jìng: feeble remorse means very weak regret after wrongdoing
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: excessive laxity is too passive an attitude towards the precepts; excessive agitation is incorrect thinking, keeping precepts without right view. Venerable Miào Jìng: the mind of regret after doing wrong is very weak — "feeble."
